description: Labelled explanation cases. Each fixes the tool output an agent was shown, the prose it produced, and the verdict a correct guard must reach. `tool_numbers` and `tool_texts` are fed to build_allowed_numbers exactly as the investigation loop feeds it the real toolkit's harvest, so these cases exercise the production guards rather than a copy of them.

cases.title: Faithful temperature explanation is accepted
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, which is 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean for this window. That places the day in the 99.8th percentile of the 1991-2020 reference distribution, an upper-tail probability of 0.0022 across 450 sampled days.

cases.title: Zero-inflated precipitation explanation is accepted
cases.note: Also checks the guard does not fire on the ordinary verb 'recorded', which contains the banned token 'record'.
cases.text: Tucson recorded 48.2 mm of precipitation. In the 1991-2020 seasonal window only 117 of 450 days were wet at all, and conditioning on those wet days gives an upper-tail probability of 0.0041.

cases.title: A negated record disclaimer is permitted
cases.note: The caveats field is supposed to say this is not an official record. If the guard flagged that, it would be unusable.
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean. This is a statistical outlier against the 1991-2020 reference distribution and not an official record; no records archive was consulted.

cases.title: Restating a probability as a percentage is permitted
cases.note: 0.22% and 1-in-455 are faithful readings of a tail probability of 0.0022, not new facts.
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C. Days at or above that level make up 0.22% of the 1991-2020 seasonal window — roughly 1 day in 455 — and the reading sits 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C mean.

cases.title: An invented percentile is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, landing in the 99.97th percentile of the 1991-2020 seasonal distribution — 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C mean.

cases.title: An inflated return period is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, a once-in-250-year reading for this seasonal window against the 1991-2020 baseline.

cases.title: A fabricated evidence row is rejected even when the prose is clean
cases.note: The prose cites only real figures; the structured evidence claims a baseline the tools never returned.
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean for the 1991-2020 window.

cases.title: An all-time claim is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, an all-time high for the city and 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean.

cases.title: Claiming a record was broken is rejected
cases.note: No records archive is consulted anywhere in this project, so any such claim is ungrounded by construction.
cases.text: At 45.6 °C, Phoenix broke its July record, finishing 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean.

cases.title: A named weather system is rejected
cases.note: No tool returns synoptic data, so naming a system is ungrounded however plausible it is.
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C as a heat dome settled over the Southwest, 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean.

cases.title: An asserted cause is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C. The reading was caused by strong subsidence and clear skies, putting it 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean.

cases.title: Citing an outside organisation is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, matching the NOAA archive for the same date and sitting 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean.

cases.title: A URL is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix reached 45.6 °C, 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean. Full series at https://example.org/phoenix-july.

cases.title: An explanation that never states the measurement is rejected
cases.text: Phoenix ran far above its seasonal mean of 41.2 °C for this window, which places the day in the 99.8th percentile of the 1991-2020 reference distribution.

cases.title: Prose about the wrong city is rejected
cases.note: Guards against a mix-up between events investigated in the same run.
cases.text: Tucson reached 45.6 °C, 4.4 °C above the 41.2 °C seasonal mean for the 1991-2020 window.
